newsitem.title: USA: Neiman Marcus to offer common shares.
newsitem.headline: Neiman Marcus to offer common shares.

text.p: Retailer Neiman Marcus Group Inc. said Wednesday it plans to offer additonal shares of its common stock to the public and use the proceeds to repurchase all of its outstanding preferred stock for about $416 million.

Neiman Marcus, which operates department stores under its name as well as under the Bergdorf Goodman marque, said it filed a registration statment with the Securities and Exchange Commission for the public offering of 8 million shares of common stock.
The company currently has about 38 million common shares outstanding.
Neiman's preferred stock is held by retailing and publishing company Harcourt General Inc., which also owns about 59 percent of Neiman's common stock.
After the transactions, in which payment for the preferred shares will be made in both cash and common stock, Harcourt will hold at least 51 percent of Neiman's common stock.
Neiman Marcus' stock fell 37.5 cents to $33 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Harcourt fell 25 cents to $53.75, also on the NYSE.
